source.prompt: (the red-tail's) A red-tailed hawk (Buteo jamaicensis), one adult bird soaring in mid-air, wings fully spread out flat to the sides and symmetrical, about 125 cm wingspan and 55 cm long, shaped to read from below and from above. Broad rounded wings with a straight leading edge and five separated, fingered primary feathers at each wingtip. Short, broad brick-red tail fanned wide into a rounded fan. Legs and feet tucked up under the body. Big rounded head and short hooked bill projecting ahead of the wings. Pale underwing with a dark leading-edge bar and a dark wrist mark, pale breast with a dark belly band. Not an eagle, not a falcon. Single bird, no base, no perch. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

rig: bird rig template, flight mesh, exactly as client/assets/redtail.glb (the client draws the raptors with the hawk's soaring and the gulls with the vulture's circling glides): PART BODY 0, TAIL 3 (pivot at the tail root), HEAD 6 (head, neck, pivot at the neck's base), WING_L/R 4/5 (the arm, pivot at the shoulder, weight ramped in over the wing root), HAND_L/R 9/10 (pivot at the wrist, weight ramped over the hand); collapse 0 (the wings never fold). extras.rig keys as the hawk's: kind 'bird', wing (shoulder [0.035, 0.11, 0.02]), wrist [0.114, 0.113, 0.02], tail [0.0, 0.097, -0.021], head [0.0, 0.107, 0.073], span_m 0.6, dihedral_deg -1.5 (shoulder to wingtip). Origin 0.11 m below the shoulder line. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Field marks: very dark slate-brown above; below heavily streaked dark brown on buff; the underwing dark with fine pale spots (lod0); the tail dark with faint narrow pale bands; a dark face and crown with an indistinct moustache and streaked buff throat; a dark bill and yellow cere. Reads as a small, very dark falcon: pointed swept wings and a dark body and wings from both sides, streaked underparts. Still open: the bill is the red-tail's hooked bill scaled (no falcon tooth, a little long); the moustache is barely separable from the dark face; the fine pale underwing spots survive on lod0 only; one size for both sexes; the paler taiga and prairie forms are not drawn.
